subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-call summary + next steps

Hi Sophie — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what I heard during our call and the recommended next steps so we can size and price properly:

Summary of needs:
- Primary use: real-time payments assistant & transaction analysis for fraud signals (inference-driven scoring + short multi-turn assistant).
- Latency target: p95 ideally < 150ms for single-turn inference; you mentioned 100–200ms goal depending on pilot thresholds.
- Throughput: steady 100 rps outside peak; peaks up to ~800 rps during settlement windows (10–15 minute bursts).
- Typical request size: ~200–600 tokens; some longer debug requests up to 1k tokens.
- Data residency: US-only; PCI/PII in requests — you will need SOC2 evidence and audit logs.

High-level recommendation:
- Pilot: Hosted API is fastest to stand up and iterate on prompts/QA.
- Production: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) is the recommended path for predictable latency and throughput at the volumes you described — can be sized to meet burst profiles and provides isolation for performance guarantees.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): likely only required if procurement requires full network isolation or a platform license; we should confirm with your security team.

Questions to validate sizing/pricing:
1) What percentage of requests are multi-turn vs single-turn (rough split)?
2) Are the peak bursts scheduled (e.g., nightly settlements) or unpredictable?
3) Any hard SLA requirements beyond the p95 latency target (uptime, RTO)?

Next steps:
- I attached a short Hosted vs Dedicated one-pager and a preliminary sizing workbook (proposed-sizing.xlsx).
- Neha (cc'd) is our Solutions Engineer — she can run a quick warm/cold-start profile and proposed capacity plan in a short technical call. Can we do a 30-min tech sync next week?

I'll hold a draft ballpark for Dedicated sizing once we get the answers above. If your procurement wants initial cost ranges for committed vs pay-as-you-go, loop them in and I can include pro forma numbers.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap, this is helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Multi-turn vs single-turn: roughly 70% single-turn scoring, 30% multi-turn assistant flows.
- Peaks: scheduled — primarily at 01:00 UTC for batch settlement windows and another smaller peak at 17:00 UTC. Peaks are fairly predictable but high intensity for 10–20 minutes.
- SLA: we need high availability during peaks; procurement will want to discuss uptime guarantees and credits, but from product side p95 < 200ms is acceptable during pilot. For production we'd like to target < 150ms.

Also: how does warm cache behave after idle periods? We are concerned about cold-starts when traffic is spiky. Can Dedicated offer faster warm starts vs Hosted?

I'll coordinate with procurement to share any constraints on committed spend.

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-call summary + next steps

Thanks Sophie — great answers, that makes sizing straightforward. Short answers to your questions and a proposed next step:

Warm/cold behavior:
- Dedicated gives you pinned capacity and much faster warm starts because model weights and KV caches remain resident on the GPU pool. For scheduled bursts (like your settlement windows) we can keep a minimal warm pool and scale up quickly.
- Hosted can handle bursts too but relies on pool autoscaling; you may see higher variance in cold-starts at the very start of a burst unless you purchase burst-prewarm credits or use a reserved warm pool.

Proposed sizing (ballpark):
- Based on 200–600 token median and peak 800 rps for short windows, a Dedicated pool equivalent to ~4x A100-class GPUs (with burst capacity) should meet p95 ~120–150ms for your mix.
- For pilot (validate model & prompts) we recommend starting on Hosted API with a provisioned warm pool for settlement windows, then transition to Dedicated with a 6–12 month commit if you want predictable unit economics.

Next steps:
1) Technical sync: Neha to run a quick profiling session (30m). Are these windows okay: Wed 3/3 10:30am PT or Thu 3/4 11:00am PT? (Scheduling link: https://cal.com/neha/30m)
2) Procurement: if you can share any commit ranges you're comfortable with, I can put together committed vs on-demand pricing scenarios in the SOW draft.

Attaching the one-pager again for your stakeholders. I'm happy to include a sample SLA language for Dedicated when procurement is ready.

Best,
Marissa
